criteria.criterion: docs/spec.toml entry OLY-B-SET-04 has a mechanism naming crates/athena-core/src/iris.rs and docs/iris-ledger.toml (not "none"), keeps owner = "Athena", and has a measure ending in 'status: not shown' or an `athena status` label, naming the test. Verify with Grep on docs/spec.toml and that the named files exist.
criteria.evidence: Grep of docs/spec.toml lines 2050-2053 shows the mechanism names both crates/athena-core/src/iris.rs and docs/iris-ledger.toml, owner = "Athena", and the measure names `cargo test -p athena-core iris` and `cargo test -p athena-core hestia` and ends in `status: not shown`. ls lists both files. The test iris_spec_entry_names_files_that_exist passed when I ran `cargo test -p athena-core iris`.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core iris`: a test shows a generation costing enough to exceed 1500 cents lifetime is refused, one within budget is allowed, and exactly 1500 cents is allowed. The refusal tests fail if the guard is removed or made to always allow.
criteria.evidence: All 7 iris tests passed. a_generation_over_the_lifetime_budget_is_refused: 1400+101 gives Err with spent, proposed and cap, and 0+1501 gives Err. a_generation_within_or_exactly_at_the_budget_is_allowed: 1400+100 and 0+1500 are allowed. I could not run a mutation because I may not edit files, and Athena's revert run removed iris.rs, so it ran 0 tests. Reading the code instead: an always-Ok guard breaks the assert_eq to Err in test (a), and `>=` in place of `>` breaks the 1400+100 and 0+1500 cases. Test (a) also calls check_against with cap u64::MAX to show the same input is allowed when there is no cap.

criteria.criterion: A test reads the committed docs/iris-ledger.toml and shows it parses, the total is at most 1500 cents, and it contains no credential-like fields; run with cargo test -p athena-core iris.
criteria.evidence: the_committed_ledger_parses_and_is_within_budget passed. It parses the committed ledger with include_str! and asserts spent_cents <= 1500. The parser refuses any key other than date, cents and note, so a credential field would make the parse fail. a_credential_or_malformed_field_is_refused passed: api_key, a top-level token, a secret field, negative, string and float cents, a missing note and malformed TOML each give an Err. The committed ledger is comments only.

findings.summary: Nothing reads the ledger file at runtime. The ledger is only read through include_str! in tests, and no function loads LEDGER_FILE from disk.
findings.evidence: iris.rs exposes parse_ledger(text) and check_generation(entries, cost) but no load_ledger(root). A future Iris client will have to add the file read itself. This is acceptable for now because no generation path exists yet, which the mechanism text, module docs and CHANGELOG all state.

findings.summary: A comment in the committed-ledger test overstates what its assertion does.
findings.evidence: The comment 'a credential-like key is an error' sits above check_generation(&entries, 0).is_ok(). The credential check actually comes from parse_ledger(...).unwrap() refusing unknown keys, not from that assertion.

summary: The change does what was asked. It adds crates/athena-core/src/iris.rs with a whole-cents lifetime budget guard: the $15 (1500-cent) cap is a constant in code, overflow is handled, and exactly the cap is allowed. The parser for the committed ledger docs/iris-ledger.toml accepts only date, cents and note, so the ledger cannot hold a credential. OLY-B-SET-04 in docs/spec.toml now names this mechanism, keeps owner Athena, and has a measure that names the tests and ends in `status: not shown`. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core iris` (7 passed) and the hestia test for OLY-B-SET-04 (passed). Athena's run of the hestia test on the reverted tree failed as it should. I could not run the iris tests without the fix, because the revert removed iris.rs, and I may not edit files. Reading the code, those tests would catch a guard that always allows and an off-by-one at the cap. The prose claims about README.md Attribution and design section 15 are true. fmt, clippy and test passed in CI. The diff touches only the six expected files, includes a CHANGELOG entry, and contains no secrets. There are two small findings: nothing reads the ledger at runtime yet, and one test comment overstates what its assertion checks.
